claims.text: Nitrogen ion implantation followed by controlled annealing will transform the near-interface region of the elemental Cr coating into graded CrN.
Implantation energies of 200–300 keV and doses of 10^16–10^17 ions/cm² are suitable for producing the intended CrN modification.
The intervention will form a thin, continuous CrN barrier at the Cr–Zr interface.
The interfacial layer will have a graded transition from pure Cr to CrN.
The graded CrN structure will minimize high-diffusivity grain boundaries.
Cr and Zr atoms have lower mobility within the nitride phase than in the unmodified coating/interface.
The CrN barrier will reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion by suppressing atomic diffusion pathways.
Post-implantation annealing will make the CrN layer uniform.
Post-implantation annealing will heal implantation-induced defects.
Healing implantation-induced defects will preserve the coating's mechanical integrity.
The modified coating will exhibit markedly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion than an unmodified elemental Cr coating.
The modified coating will have better oxidation resistance than the unmodified elemental Cr coating.
Reduced interdiffusion and retained oxidation resistance will enhance coating durability.
The durability benefit will apply under subcritical water at approximately 320 °C and 11–12 MPa for extended durations.
The durability benefit will apply in steam at approximately 1200 °C for about 5 hours.
An unmodified elemental Cr coating undergoes significant Cr–Zr interdiffusion during high-temperature steam exposure.
An unmodified elemental Cr coating undergoes oxidation-induced degradation during high-temperature steam exposure.
Precisely controlled implantation and annealing can modify the Cr coating without altering or damaging the underlying zirconium alloy.

contradictions.description: The target is described as the near-interface region and specifically the buried Cr–Zr interface, but the conditions instead say that implantation selectively transforms the surface layer of the Cr coating. The spatial location of the proposed CrN layer is therefore inconsistent or insufficiently resolved.

The hypothesis and mechanism say oxidation resistance is maintained, whereas the predicted outcome claims it is improved relative to the unmodified coating. Preservation and improvement are distinct predictions.
